title: Role readiness activation scorecard + async interview rubric (WIP)
content:
Purpose:

This working doc is a compact, reusable template combining: (1) a role-readiness activation scorecard to standardize hire decisions and first-30/60/90 impact milestones; (2) an asynchronous interview/work-sample rubric for distributed hiring; and (3) a lightweight onboarding mini-sprint checklist to ensure rapid ramp. The main goal is to reduce subjectivity across interviewers and give hiring managers clear, observable ramp expectations post-offer.

Scope and intended use:
- Use for IC and senior IC roles across eng, product, and infra where a work-sample or async exercise is appropriate.
- Designed to plug into existing interview loops: replace one live take-home plus one panel with this async rubric + a 30-min sync.
- Treat as a living doc: collect data after each hire and iterate scoring anchors quarterly.

How teams should use this file (quick steps):
1) Hiring manager picks core competencies (must pick 3–5).
2) People ops attaches the scorecard to the JD and the async task.
3) Interviewers score independently in the hiring kit; aggregated score guides hiring decision.
4) If hire is made, scorecard seeds the 30/60/90 mini-sprint for the manager and mentor.

Part A — Role Readiness Activation Scorecard (single-sheet)
Fields to fill before interviews (hiring manager):
- Role name: [text]
- Seniority band: [IC2/IC3/IC4/etc]
- Hiring priority: [High/Medium/Low]
- Core competencies (pick 3–5): e.g., System design, Production debugging, Cross-team communication, ML inference optimization
- Critical deliverable in first 90 days: [single sentence]
- Success metric for 90 days: [quantifiable where possible]

Scorecard layout and explanation (scored 1–5 for each competency, also weight):
- Competency label (weight %): numeric score 1–5 and brief evidence note.
- Overall readiness index = weighted average of competency scores (round to nearest tenth).
- Recommendation thresholds (example): >=4.2 strong hire; 3.5–4.19 proceed with caution/comp plan; 3.0–3.49 consider alternate candidate or extended trial; <3.0 no hire.

Scoring anchors (compact):
1 = No observable ability / answers show fundamental gaps.
2 = Basic familiarity; would need heavy ramp and close coaching.
3 = Solid working competency; capable with normal onboarding.
4 = Strong; can independently deliver the listed critical deliverable with minimal help.
5 = Exceptional; has led similar work and can mentor others.

Example competency row (text):
- System design (weight 30%): 4 — Proposed a design that balances latency and cost, included KV-caching option, tradeoffs discussed.

Decision rubric (combine scores + behavioral anchors):
- Hire: readiness index >=4.2 AND no major culture/communication red flags.
- Hire with conditions: 3.8–4.19 OR lower index but compensating evidence (e.g., exceptional domain experience). Conditions include 60-day success plan or mentor pairing.
- Trial/Contract: 3.2–3.79 and manager willing to sponsor a 3-month paid trial.
- Reject: <3.2 OR unresolved integrity/ethics/intellectual-fit concerns.

Part B — Asynchronous Interview / Work-Sample Rubric
Goals for async exercise:
- Measure applied problem solving relevant to the role (not just algorithmic puzzles).
- Observe tradeoff reasoning, communication clarity, and reproducible outputs.
- Keep time budget 3–6 hours for mid-senior roles; communicate expectations clearly.

Candidate deliverable template to send: (example for infra/serving-runtime hire)
- Short README (max 500 words): restate the problem and scope you chose.
- Artefact: runnable code or a clear design doc with mocks/screenshots.
- Clear instructions to run any demo, plus test cases or perf summary if applicable.
- Short video (optional, 3–5 minutes) walking through approach and tradeoffs.

Async rubric axes (score each 1–5 with short evidence note):
- Problem framing (weight 20%): Did candidate restate scope, assumptions, and success criteria?
- Technical correctness & completeness (weight 30%): Does the solution work and cover edge cases?
- Tradeoffs & systems thinking (weight 25%): Were latency/cost/operational constraints considered?
- Communication & reproducibility (weight 15%): Is the README clear and can reviewers run the artefact?
- Ownership & production-readiness (weight 10%): Tests, monitoring hooks, rollback plan?

Async rubric anchors (examples):
- Problem framing 5: Candidate succinctly narrowed scope, enumerated assumptions, defined metrics for success.
- Tradeoffs 3: Candidate mentioned caching as possibility but did not quantify cost/latency trade.

Interview instructions for candidates (to include in task email):
- Time estimate: 4 hours. Tell us if you spent more.
- We value clarity: include a 3–5 line TL;DR and a 2–3 minute voice note or short video.
- Acceptable artefacts: Git repo link, zip, or PDF design with diagrams.
- Submission window: 72 hours.
- We will not grade on styling; focus on reasoning and measurable outcomes.

Reviewer guidance and calibration (people ops):
- Two reviewers minimum: one hiring manager and one cross-functional engineer.
- Independent scoring required before discussion.
- Use evidence-first notes: link to exact lines or sections that justify the score.
- If reviewer scores differ by >1.5 on any axis, schedule a 30-minute calibration meeting.

Part C — Behavioral / Culture Rubric (short)
Target anchors: collaboration, feedback orientation, customer empathy.
Scoring 1–5 with quick examples expected in notes.
- 5: Provided concrete stories showing influence across teams, took measurable feedback, iterated on deliverable.
- 3: Gave reasonable examples with limited measurable outcome.
- 1: Vague or no examples; cannot articulate role in team outcomes.

Sample behavioral prompts (for async or short sync):
- Tell us about a time you found a performance regression in production. What steps did you take?
- Describe an instance where you changed another team’s approach through persuasion or data.
- When have you had to compromise between shipping and long-term maintainability?

Part D — Onboarding mini-sprint (first 30/60/90 condensed checklist)
Purpose: Translate scorecard to concrete first-30 work to show momentum and make decision points visible.
Pre-boarding (before day 1):
- Manager sets up access, dev environment checklist, first-week reading list, and first-ticket ready. Owner: Manager and SRE buddy.
Day 0–7 (Orientation + quick wins):
- 1: Intro to codebase + run tests locally (owner: mentor).
- 2: Small production-adjacent task (bugfix or doc update) with PR within week.
- 3: 1:1 alignment meeting to set 30-day priority.
Day 8–30 (Delivery & feedback):
- Complete the critical first-ticket tied to the role-readiness scorecard.
- Weekly async check-ins: candidate posts brief status + blockers in hiring channel.
- Manager/mentor check at day 14 and day 30 to compare against success metric.
60 days:
- Candidate should own a cross-team touchpoint (incidence postmortem or perf tuning).
90 days:
- Candidate delivers on the critical 90-day deliverable or an agreed milestone.

Success criteria examples to include in offer doc: concrete targets (e.g., reduce median tail latency for endpoint X by 15% under baseline test).

Manager playbook for conditional hires/trials:
- If hire with conditions: attach 60-day success plan and weekly review slots.
- If trial/contract: define deliverables, payment cadence, and conversion evaluation checklist.

Data collection & metrics (people ops):
- Track: time-to-hire, async-task completion rate, score distribution by interviewer, hire conversion rate, first-90 outcome (pass/needs-improvement).
- Run quarterly calibration sessions for hiring managers and top contributors to maintain rubric alignment.

Open questions & next steps (WIP):
- Pilot this flow for two infra and two product roles in Q4 and collect conversion + manager satisfaction.
- Draft a short candidate-facing one-pager describing the async loop and time commitment.
- Create a templated feedback form to capture reviewer evidence more consistently.

Quick templates to copy into emails (short):
- Candidate email subject: "Redwood Inference: async task for <role> — 72-hour window"
- Candidate TL;DR note: "This exercise is designed to see applied decision-making. Expect ~4 hours. We value reasoning over polish. Links to sample outputs and rubric are attached."

Notes and provenance:
- Inspired by distributed hiring best practices and our need to reduce interviewer load while keeping rigorous evaluation for production-facing roles.
- Will iterate based on pilot outcomes.

Document history and contributors:

End of document.
